name: iLovePDF Premium
subcategory: PDF editing, document workflows and electronic signatures
tagline: Merge, split, compress, convert, and annotate PDFs without uploading them to a vendor

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: Examples per task: merge 25 files/100 MB; compress 2 files/200 MB; most Office conversions 1 file/15 MB; image-to-PDF 20 files/40 MB; sign 3 files/50 MB; redact/compare up to 400 MB

tiers.name: Premium
tiers.limits: Unlimited document processing overall; task caps commonly 10 files or 4 GB (tool-specific); 2,000 AI credits; 5 advanced eSignatures; web, desktop and mobile
tiers.notes: Annual total is $60; monthly plan is $9

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: 25+ users; custom AI credits and advanced-signature allowance; SSO, dedicated manager, custom contract

pricing.freeTierCaps: Tool-specific: merge 25 files/100 MB; compress 2/200 MB; most conversions 1/15 MB; image-to-PDF 20/40 MB; sign 3/50 MB; redact and compare 2/400 MB; no AI credits
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (Premium $9 monthly or $60/year = $5/month; annual is 42% lower); Business custom
pricing.hiddenCosts: Premium includes 2,000 AI credits and only 5 advanced eSignatures; Business pricing is quote-only; adding/removing licenses adjusts the subscription

verdictSummary: The core loop is small enough for a capable coding agent to produce a useful local version in one sitting. For ILovePDF Premium, merge, split, compress, convert, and annotate PDFs without uploading them to a vendor. The hard boundary is simple hosted delivery, mobile apps, desktop tools, ocr, and batch capacity, plus document fidelity, identity, and compliance.
coreLoopDIY: Merge, split, compress, convert, and annotate PDFs locally, preserve originals, generate auditable outputs, and keep files in a user-owned store without uploading them to a vendor.
whatYouLose: simple hosted delivery, mobile apps, desktop tools, OCR, and batch capacity
replacementScope: personal document tool or low-stakes signature flow
ongoingBurden: format edge cases, fonts, rendering, encryption, signatures, evidence, retention, storage, backups, and legal requirements
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for ILovePDF Premium because the visible editor is reproducible, but reliable rendering and legally defensible signature workflows are not a casual side project. The recurring cost buys format edge cases, fonts, rendering, encryption, signatures, evidence, retention, storage, backups, and legal requirements, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Stirling PDF
priorArt.desc: Active open-source web application for a broad set of PDF operations.

alternatives.name: PDF24
alternatives.desc: Nearly every common PDF transformation is free and unmetered; Windows users also get an offline desktop suite.

facts.install: Use the hosted tools in a browser, or install PDF24 Creator for offline use on Windows
facts.dataFormat: PDF24 Creator processes documents locally on Windows; web-tool uploads are encrypted in transit, processed on PDF24's servers in Germany, and automatically deleted after about one hour
facts.gapVsPaid: The private desktop route is Windows-only, while using its otherwise convenient web tools still means uploading documents to PDF24's servers.
facts.setupBlocker: The private offline desktop suite is Windows-only; other operating systems must use the upload-based web tools

alternatives.name: PDFgear
alternatives.desc: A polished free editor and converter with local desktop and mobile apps; fewer batch and server workflows than Stirling PDF.

facts.install: Install the Windows, macOS, iOS, or Android app, or open the browser-based secure tools
facts.engines: Ordinary PDF editing and OCR are local; the optional PDF Copilot uses OpenAI/ChatGPT-family language models
facts.dataFormat: Desktop documents remain local, and the secure browser tools say processing happens client-side; using PDF Copilot sends the document content and questions needed for the answer to OpenAI
facts.gapVsPaid: It is polished for individual files, but offers fewer bulk, server, and automation workflows than the broad iLovePDF service.

alternatives.name: Stirling PDF
alternatives.desc: The private iLovePDF answer: merge, split, compress, convert, OCR, annotate, redact, and batch-process without feeding documents to somebody else's cloud.

facts.install: Install the native Windows/macOS desktop build, run the Linux JAR, or deploy the documented Docker image/Compose stack; a hosted cloud edition also exists
facts.dataFormat: Desktop and self-hosted deployments process files on the user's machine/server and can use mounted local storage; the cloud edition uploads files for transient server processing
facts.gapVsPaid: It removes the vendor-upload problem, but a private cross-platform deployment asks the user to install and maintain a desktop build or Docker service instead of opening a website.
facts.setupBlocker: The native desktop app is simple, but a full private cross-platform service and automation setup is most reliably deployed with Docker

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Premium plan and a personal document tool or low-stakes signature flow DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for ILovePDF Premium in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, Python 3.12, FastAPI, pikepdf, LibreOffice headless, and PostgreSQL; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: merge, split, compress, convert, and annotate PDFs locally, preserve originals, generate auditable outputs, and keep files in a user-owned store without uploading them to a vendor.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Keep every original immutable and write each operation to a versioned output file.
Support merge, split, reorder, rotate, compress, watermark, redact, OCR, and Office-to-PDF conversion.
Render page previews and warn when fonts, forms, signatures, or encryption may be altered.
For signature mode, place fields, invite signers, record consent, and seal a final PDF hash.
Maintain an append-only event log with timestamps, document hashes, and delivery outcomes.
Add file expiry, download, deletion, backup, and a prominent low-stakes-use warning.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out qualified or regulated electronic signatures.
Deliberately leave out government identity verification.
Deliberately leave out full Acrobat-level editing and enterprise document governance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
